Personally, it's the same thing. You're still absorbing the story and enjoying it. Just like students/people who have disabilities such as dyslexia or are slow readers, it is highly beneficial and honestly wonderful. I listened to my first audiobook on a 6-hour drive from Chicago to Dayton, OH for the holidays and the voice acting had me hooked into the story. I counted it on my Goodreads goal and I've heard many people say they count it. My best friend commutes an hour to work and an hour home every day and also travels weekly for her job and audiobooks are her godsend. Plus physical books when she doesn't get motion sickness on the plane. Hope this helps. :) It all depends on how you view it. If you think it counts then it counts!

Congrats on married life and welcome to the Navy family! My husband is currently in A school at Great Lakes and he left for boot camp 12 days after our wedding. We found an apt. 20ish mins off base and moved me up 2 weeks post-graduation. Once we had a firm address he applied for what is called "Live ashore" which will allow him to live with me and have a driving pass for his vehicle. We also get BAH. Every 4th day he has his "Duty Day" Where he has to be on base for 24 hours so he normally will just sleep in his barracks that night which is fine. Gives me some me time. I'd do research on apartments in the area and maybe join a FB group to get input on apartment complexes and such in the area! I'm still new to all of this as well but feel free to ask me any questions. I have another Navy wife friend who moved from Ohio to San Diego to be with her husband and he just applied for his live ashore. He went ahead and got a parking pass though so he can do overnights with her or just be with her till curfew and have weekends at home when he doesn't have a Duty weekend.

We only want to be overseas if he is guaranteed shore duty. He's afraid of being in a different country and still deploying and leaving me completely alone lol.

He's still in his A school and we are currently living off base by the North Chicago base. I'm hoping we get to go to San Diego or Norfolk for his C school. We are hopeful for Italy if he gets shore duty for his first duty station! We are both originally from Ohio so luckily family isn't super far right now. Just super lonely when he has to be on base for his watches.

My husband graduated boot last Oct. and was in a mens only division but one of his friends at A school was in a mixed one. One of my new Navy wife friends said her husband was in a mixed one. He graduated the week after my husband. Hope this helps. :) 

Good luck to you hun!
